serialization.attr_key_order_note: attr key order as resolved by the schema; the editor emits attrs in this order, Import may differ -> compare canonicalised (sorted-key) JSON

normalization.evidence: 既有真机帧 (docs/office-collab-protocol-spike.md §3: Import content.data vs editor fetch doc.data, 36 raw diffs -> 3 normalised) + SPK 束内模块 (schema round-trip is byte-exact, see normalization_verification.json)
normalization.direction: Office.Import (OOXML -> .odoc) omits attributes that equal the schema default; the editor toJSON() always emits REQUIRED attrs and omits OPTIONAL attrs equal to their empty_value. Canonicalise by applying the schema rule below, not by guessing.

rules.applies_to: every node attr declared with `optional:false` (default in `.default`)
rules.rule: if the attr (or a composite sub-field) is absent, insert its `.default`; these attrs are ALWAYS present in the editor fetch JSON
rules.status: schema-backed (SPK 束内模块) — proven by byte-exact round-trip

rules.applies_to: every node attr declared with `optional:true` (default in `.empty_value`)
rules.rule: do NOT insert these when absent; and when comparing against editor output, drop them if they equal `empty_value`. Inserting them (as a naive "fill all defaults" pass does) CREATES diffs instead of removing them.
rules.status: schema-backed (SPK 束内模块) — the naive fill-all-defaults variant produced 105 diffs, see normalization_verification.json

rules.rule: Import emits `attrs:{}` / `content:[]` explicitly; the editor omits them. Drop `attrs` when it ends up empty and `content` when it is [].

rules.applies_to: `@C_text/comment` BSON section (not part of the doc JSON)
rules.rule: Import writes `{"data":[],"format":1}`; the editor snapshot writes `{"data":[]}` (runner.js omits `format`).

canonicalisation_algorithm: 1. parse the doc JSON (from BSON @C_text/content.data or from the `fetch` ack)
2. for every node, look up its node type in doc_schema.json
3. for each attr (and composite `deep` sub-field) with optional:false, if absent set it to `.default`
4. drop attrs whose optional:true value equals `empty_value`; drop `attrs` if it becomes empty
5. drop `content` when it is an empty array
6. serialise with sorted keys + no whitespace, then sha256
NOTE: the strongest correctness check is not this algorithm but `schema.nodeFromJSON(x).toJSON()` — that is byte-exact (see normalization_verification.json)

minimal_verification.manual_cross_check: open the two JSON files side by side at `$.content[0].attrs` and `$.attrs.page_setup`: the Import copy has `{}` / no `orientation`, the fetch copy has all six page_setup fields including `"orientation":"portrait"`.
